html:
The Wuthathi, also known as the Mutjati, are an Aboriginal Australian people of the eastern coast of the northern Cape York Peninsula in Queensland, around Shelburne Bay. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

The anthropologist Norman Tindale treated the Mutjati and the Otati as two peoples, while the Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies treats both names as one group, the Wuthathi. Little else is recorded of their early history. Neighbours on the map include the Anggamudi, the Kuuku Ya'u and the Mpalitjanh. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
